title: AI Companies Are Recruiting Electricians and Carpenters By the Thousands - Slashdot

content_html:
An anonymous reader quotes a New York Times report on how AI companies are pouring money into training and recruiting electricians, carpenters, and other skilled tradespeople to build data centers: There is no parallel in American history for the boom underway in the construction of data centers, fueled by companies with functionally unlimited cash that are racing to supply skyrocketing demand for their A.I. models. The explosion has offset flagging activity in other sectors, like office construction, which never recovered after the pandemic. Housing has been depressed by high interest rates, and offshore wind felled by political opposition. Still, competition for labor -- never mind land and materials -- is starting to weigh on other parts of the industry.

"There's no question the resources are very limited, so decisions to build one thing kind of drag from another," said Mario Iacobacci, who runs the construction and infrastructure advisory practice at Oxford Economics. Developers are paying a premium for workers, especially in the rural areas where they are building data centers. According to an analysis by Indeed, the job listings website, hourly installation and maintenance jobs at data centers pay 42 percent more than similar jobs in other fields. Behind that inflated pay is a bidding war. In markets with a lot of data center construction, like Dallas and Northern Virginia, workers can jump ship for bonuses or higher per diem rates. The competition has driven contractors to staffing services like Aerotek.

"It is creating a labor tension that is really delicate," said Marty Schager, Aerotek's director of data center market development. "You've got a passive job-seeker community out there right now that I think is looking to potentially capture opportunity with this once-in-a-generation data center gold rush." [...] The question looms over the apprentices who will become journeymen as the build-out reaches fever pitch. Fully trained electricians could shift to nuclear plants, apartment buildings or pharmaceutical factories. But it's hard to imagine anything on the scale of what's underway.

"The best-case scenario would be you train all these skilled workers up and right when the data centers start to become less popular is we'd have a housing boom," said Jeff Strohl, director of Georgetown University's Center on Education and the Workforce. "That's probably not likely."

"If we have an influx of workers at this point with the data centers being built, what happens when they're done? Where do those workers go?" he said. "How many people does it take to run a data center after taking up all this property and all this land that could have been used for something else?"

一位匿名读者引用了《纽约时报》的一篇报道，介绍了人工智能公司如何投入大量资金培训和招聘电工、木匠和其他熟练技工来建设数据中心：数据中心建设的热潮在美国历史上是史无前例的，由拥有无限现金的公司推动，这些公司竞相满足其人工智能的飙升需求。 模型。 爆炸性增长抵消了其他行业的低迷活动，例如办公楼建筑，这些行业在大流行后从未恢复。 高利率抑制了房地产市场，政治反对派也削弱了海上风电。 尽管如此，劳动力竞争——更不用说土地和材料——正开始对该行业的其他部分造成压力。 牛津经济研究院负责建筑和基础设施咨询业务的马里奥·亚科巴奇 (Mario Iacobacci) 表示：“毫无疑问，资源非常有限，因此建造一件事的决定会受到另一件事的拖累。” 开发商为工人支付了高价，尤其是在他们正在建设数据中心的农村地区。 根据招聘网站 Indeed 的分析，数据中心按小时计算的安装和维护工作的薪资比其他领域的类似工作高出 42%。 高薪的背后是一场竞购战。 在达拉斯和北弗吉尼亚州等拥有大量数据中心建设的市场，员工可以跳槽以获得奖金或更高的每日津贴。 竞争促使承包商转向 Aerotek 等人力资源服务公司。 Aerotek 数据中心市场开发总监 Marty Schager 表示：“这造成了非常微妙的劳动力紧张局势。” “现在有一个被动的求职者社区，我认为他们正在寻找潜在的机会，通过这个千载难逢的数据中心淘金热抓住机会。” [...] 随着扩建达到高潮，学徒们将成为熟练工，这个问题笼罩在他们身上。 训练有素的电工可以转移到核电站、公寓楼或制药厂。 但很难想象正在发生的事情的规模。 乔治城大学教育和劳动力中心主任杰夫·斯特罗尔表示：“最好的情况是培训所有这些技术工人，当数据中心开始变得不那么受欢迎时，我们就会出现房地产繁荣。” “这可能不太可能。”

“如果数据中心正在建设中，我们现在有大量工人涌入，那么完工后会发生什么？ 那些工人去哪儿了？” 他说。 “在占用了所有这些财产和所有这些本来可以用于其他用途的土地之后，需要多少人来运营一个数据中心？”
